question.text: The US also occupied this country after the Spanish-American War, though they did not annex it. The CIA tried to use an exploding cigar and a tuberculosis-infected scuba suit to kill Fidel Castro, a Communist who led this country during the Cold War.
question.clue: The Teller Amendment asserted the independence of this country, which had previously tried to gain independence in the Little War and the Ten Years' War.

swap.leadin: He met with Jose de San Martin at the Guayaquil Conference.
swap.text: Name this early 19th-century South American leader nicknamed "The Liberator."
swap.clue: With his ally Francisco de Santander, this man won the Battle of Boyaca to complete his conquering of the Viceroyalty of New Granada.

question.leadin: Former secretary of state John Kerry claimed that this country was a "narco-kleptocracy."
question.text: Name this Central American country once led by Manuel Noriega that separated from Colombia in 1903. It was invaded by the United States in Operation Just Cause in 1989.
question.clue: Operation Nifty Package sunk the boat of a leader of this country, who subsequently hid in its Vatican diplomatic mission.

swap.text: In the 17th and 18th centuries, galleon trade flourished between Manila and this Mexican city, whose bay forms a notable beach resort today.
swap.clue: This Mexican port city. Under the rule of New Spain, it was granted a monopoly on the Manila galleon trade.

question.leadin: Historically, this country was part of a territory called the Banda Oriental.
question.text: Name this South American country that gained independence as a result of the Cisplatine War. Bruno Mauricio de Zabala founded this country's capital Montevideo.
question.clue: This country was riven for years by civil war between its Red and White Parties, and a guerrilla group named for an Incan rebel leader operated in this country.

swap.text: One of Bolivia's capitals is named after this Venezuelan lieutenant of Bolivar, who helped him win at the Battle of Ayacucho and succeeded him as President of Bolivia.
swap.clue: After being defeated at the second battle of Huachi, he won a victory over the army of Melchor Aymerich which allowed him to put down resistance in the Pasto province.

question.leadin: The control of this country's First Republic by two wealthy states led to it being nicknamed for their main products, "coffee and milk."
question.text: Name this country, where that republic was founded by disciples of the positivist sociologist Auguste Comte. This country was later ruled by the populist dictator Getulio Vargas.
question.answerHtml: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil; accept First Brazilian Republic; accept Republic of the United States of Brazil; prompt on Old Republic]
question.clue: Black and indigenous militia leaders took a leading role in expelling a Dutch takeover of this colony in the mid-17th century.

swap.text: This Liberal leader in the Reform War assumed power after the war's conclusion. This Zapotec [ZAH-po-tek] politician served five terms as Mexico's president.
swap.clue: As minister of justice under Igancio Comonfort, he issued a namesake law which restricted the roles of the church and army in government.

question.leadin: Name these countries in which communist insurgencies took place.
question.text: Maurice Bishop's New Jewel Movement seized this country in 1979 and ruled until ousted by a further left government in 1983. Shortly after, the U.S. and the Organization of East Caribbean States invaded and restored parliamentary government.
question.clue: This island was captured from Lord Macartney by the French during the Revolutionary War and was the site of a naval battle between the grandfather of Lord Byron and the Comte d'Estaing.

swap.text: Revolting twice against Sebastian Lerdo, he took power in 1877 and served as president twice before resigning in 1911 and going into exile.
swap.clue: Reforms under this leader were promulgated by technocratic cientificos such as Jose Yves Limantour.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a 2010 incident.
question.text: Outside the Copiapo hospital where the miners were monitored after excavation, this Chilean President made a public declaration that mine safety conditions would be reviewed. He was present as each of the miners emerged.

swap.text: A cardinal from this country, Ernesto Cardenal, responded to the criticism of liberation theology by declaring "I do not think the Pope understands Marxism." Cardenal earlier opposed this country's Somoza dictatorship.
swap.clue: Somoza eventually fled the country and seceded power to the Junta of National Reconstruction, who fought a civil war with The Sandinista National Liberation Front.

question.text: The PRI's poor handling of the earthquake was one of the reasons that led Cuauhtemoc ("kwa-ooh-tay-mok"), a member of this family, to run against it as part of the PRD. An earlier president of Mexico with this surname nationalized the country's oil industry to create Pemex.
question.clue: This surname of a PRD candidate for president. Another politician with this surname exiled Plutarco Elias Calles ("ploo-TARK-oh eh-LEE-as kai-EZ").

swap.leadin: Bartolome de Las Casas lamented the unnecessary deaths of natives in this system before they were able to understand "the true faith or sacraments."
swap.text: Name this system of colonial labor, which Las Casas called a "moral pestilence." This system, akin to slavery, awarded the labor of indigenous peoples to the Spanish colonial elite.
swap.clue: Despite the fact that religious orders retained control over all lands under its jurisdiction, reformers like Bartolome de las Casas sought to eliminate all systems under which natives were assimilated.

question.leadin: The special forces unit Search Bloc was established to target this man, who for a time led his organization from a private resort-prison called La Catedral.
question.text: Identify this man who may have been behind M-19's 1985 siege of the Palace of Justice after working with the Ochoa Vasquez brothers to found the infamous Medellin drug cartel.
question.clue: This man agreed to a period of nominal captivity at La Catedral prison in exchange for a deal preventing his extradition to the U.S.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about a revolution.
swap.text: Published in 1938 by the Trinidadian writer C.L.R. James, this book was the first history of the Haitian Revolution told from the perspective of the revolutionaries.
swap.clue: This history of the Haitian Revolution written by C.L.R. James linked the Haitian struggle with the French Revolution and its ideals.

question.text: The Paraguayan forces were led by this general, who later served as Paraguayan president before being killed in a 1940 air crash. He drove Paraguayan forces into Bolivian territory, where the war stalled.

swap.text: Anger at the Somozas grew thanks to reporting by La Prensa, which this person edited after her husband was murdered in 1978. This politician beat Daniel Ortega in 1990 to become Nicaragua's first female president.
swap.clue: This woman who ran the opposition newspaper La Prensa after her husband Pedro was assassinated by the Somoza regime. She was later elected President of Nicaragua in 1990.

question.leadin: Edward Bernays was hired to convince Congress that this law was blatantly Communist, despite the fact that its express purpose was to foster a capitalist economy in place of actual feudalism.
question.text: Identify this 1952 act that massively redistributed land in its country, the most significant reform during a period known as the Ten Years of Spring.
question.answerHtml: Decree 900 [or Decreto 900; prompt on the Agrarian Reform Law; prompt on descriptive answers]
question.clue: This was the name of the 1952 law supported by Jacobo Arbenz that any unused private land should be redistributed to peasant farmers.

swap.leadin: The newspaper El Dia "became the conscience" of this party.
swap.text: Name this party that held power during the rule of Don Pepe Batlle, an advocate of Krausismo.
swap.clue: A "defense government" led by a party of this name endured a nine year siege during a war which saw that party aided by an "Italian Legion" led by Garibaldi.
